title: Medical benchmark shows strong model scores—and why they are not clinical proof
friendlyTitle: AI models scored well on hard medical questions, but the test has limits
summary: Natomy tested leading models zero-shot on MedXpertQA, including 2,000 questions with clinical images and 2,450 text-only questions. Gemini 3.8 Flash led the reported single runs, but the authors flag duplicated answer choices, occasional contradictory questions, image problems, exact-match grading and small subgroup samples.
friendlySummary: Several models answered expert medical questions, including questions with images. The results came from single runs, and the test data and grading sometimes had problems.
whyItMatters: A high exam score can help teams choose models for further evaluation, but it does not establish safe diagnosis or treatment performance with real patients. Healthcare buyers need repeated tests, representative clinical data, workflow-specific error analysis and qualified human oversight.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A good quiz score does not prove that an AI is safe for patient care. Hospitals still need real clinical tests, careful error checks and trained people in charge.
